sections.heading: What Is an Insulated Glass Unit and Why Does It Fail?
sections.body: An insulated glass unit, commonly called an IGU, consists of two or more panes of glass separated by a sealed airspace filled with air or an inert gas such as argon. This sealed construction is what gives modern windows their thermal and acoustic performance. Over time, the perimeter seal that holds everything together can break down due to temperature cycling, moisture exposure, physical stress, or simple age. Once the seal fails, outside air and humidity infiltrate the airspace, causing the telltale foggy or hazy appearance between the panes that cannot be cleaned from the inside. In a busy commercial environment like the properties surrounding Tysons Galleria or the office towers along Route 123, a compromised IGU can also allow uncomfortable drafts and outside noise to penetrate the interior. Replacing the glass unit rather than the entire window frame is usually the most cost-effective and least disruptive path forward for both property managers and homeowners.

sections.heading: Signs Your Tysons Property Needs IGU Replacement
sections.body: Knowing when to call for insulated glass unit replacement in Tysons can save you from more extensive repairs down the road. The most obvious indicator is condensation or fogging trapped between the panes — a clear sign the seal has failed and the insulating gas has escaped. You may also notice visible moisture streaks, a milky residue, or a distorted reflection on the glass surface. Beyond appearance, a failed IGU often translates to noticeable temperature differences near the window, drafts that weren't there before, or increased difficulty maintaining a consistent indoor climate. Commercial tenants in Tysons Corner's busy retail and office spaces may also report increased outside noise as a symptom of degraded glazing performance. For residential clients in nearby neighborhoods, the first sign is often a spike in heating or cooling discomfort. Any of these symptoms warrant a professional assessment to determine whether the IGU can be replaced independently or whether the frame and surrounding components also need attention.

faq.q: How do I know if I need an IGU replacement or a full window replacement?
faq.a: In many cases, if the window frame itself is structurally sound and in good condition, only the insulated glass unit needs to be replaced — not the entire window assembly. A technician can assess the frame, hardware, and surrounding components during an on-site visit and recommend the most appropriate and cost-effective solution for your specific situation.

faq.q: How long does insulated glass unit replacement typically take?
faq.a: For most standard residential IGU replacements, the work can often be completed in a single visit once the replacement unit has been fabricated to the correct specifications. Commercial projects with multiple units or custom glass may require additional lead time for fabrication. We will give you a realistic timeline during the assessment so you can plan accordingly.

faq.q: Can you match the existing glass type, tint, or coating on my current windows?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. We work to match existing glass specifications as closely as possible, including thickness, tint, and low-emissivity or reflective coatings. Bringing accurate measurements and, where possible, information about the original window manufacturer helps us source the best match for your property.
